items.label: Brent crude
items.why: India imports about 85% of its oil. Costlier crude widens the trade deficit, weakens the rupee, lifts inflation and hurts oil marketing, paint, airline and chemical companies.

items.label: WTI crude
items.why: A fall lowers India's import bill.

items.label: Gold
items.why: Falling gold usually means investors are comfortable taking risk.

items.label: US 10-year yield
items.why: Higher US yields make US bonds more attractive than emerging-market stocks, which tends to pull FII money out of India.

items.label: US dollar index
items.why: A stronger dollar usually means money flowing out of emerging markets, including India.

items.label: USD / INR
items.why: A weaker rupee (higher USD/INR) cuts FII returns in dollar terms and makes imports costlier. It helps IT and pharma exporters.

items.label: India 10-year yield
items.why: Rising Indian yields raise borrowing costs and compete with equities, especially for banks' bond books and rate-sensitive sectors.

items.label: S&P 500
items.why: Global risk appetite is improving; Indian markets usually follow over time.

items.label: US VIX (fear gauge)
items.why: Calm US markets support risk-taking globally.

fed.why: The Fed has raised rates over the last six months, which tends to pull money back to the US.
